text:
Tomas Hertl has been one of Vegas's most effective forwards at 5v5. In 15.7 minutes a night he has 10 goals and 20 points in 25 games, and with him on the ice the Golden Knights have 63.3% of the expected goals, the share of chance quality for and against.

None of it leans on luck. His 10 goals come on 11.4 expected, his own chances are up to 1.74 expected goals per 60 from 1.51 last season, and his 15.6% shooting sits just above his talent range. The last ten games were his best: five goals and 12 points against 7.3 expected, with two-goal nights against Pittsburgh and Buffalo.

The style is heavier than the minutes suggest: 64 hits, and a top shot of 91.7 mph, 94th percentile in NHL Edge tracking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 32% of his entries last season while still setting up 8.2 primary shot assists per 60. Jesse Granger of The Athletic summed up the physical side after the first Dallas game: "Esa Lindell tried to hit Tomas Hertl, and it looked like he ran into a metal pole."
